#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

# Remove any existing experiment directory and recreate sample structure
rm -rf experiment
mkdir -p experiment/dirA experiment/dirB/subdirB experiment/dirC

# Non-.txt file
cat > experiment/README.md <<'EOF'
This is a README and should not be counted.
EOF

# .txt files (some contain the sample keyword "apple")
cat > experiment/file1.txt <<'EOF'
apple banana
line two
apple again
EOF

cat > experiment/dirA/file2.txt <<'EOF'
no keyword here
just some text
EOF

cat > experiment/dirA/file3.txt <<'EOF'
this contains apple once
EOF

cat > experiment/dirB/subdirB/file4.txt <<'EOF'
apple
apple
apple
EOF

apple in log should be ignored (.log)
EOF

echo "Sample 'experiment' directory created."
BASH

# Create counting script
cat > count_lines.sh <<'BASH'
#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

if [ "$#" -ne 1 ]; then
  echo "Usage: $0 keyword"
  exit 1
fi
keyword=$1

# Sum lines of all .txt files under 'experiment' that contain at least one occurrence of the keyword.
# For safety, handle the case where no files match.
total=0
while IFS= read -r -d '' file; do
  lines=$(wc -l < "$file")
  total=$((total + lines))
done < <(grep -rlZ --include='*.txt' -- "$keyword" experiment || true)

echo "$total"
BASH

chmod +x generate_experiment.sh count_lines.sh

# Create the sample experiment structure right away for convenience
./generate_experiment.sh

# Show the created structure
ls -R experiment

# Show the two scripts created (first 200 lines each to keep output short)
printf "\n--- generate_experiment.sh ---\n"
sed -n '1,200p' generate_experiment.sh
printf "\n--- count_lines.sh ---\n"
sed -n '1,200p' count_lines.sh
"}
